chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: al-Ash'ath ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to us, he said: Shu'ayb ibn Umar narrated to me, from his father, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said:

I visited Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), and his brother Zayd (peace be upon him) was with him. Then Ma'ruf ibn Kharbudh al-Makki entered, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "O Ma'ruf, recite for me some of the gems of your poetry." So he recited: "By your life, Abu Malik is neither feeble nor weak in his strength, nor obstinate in his speech opposing the wise one when he forbids him. But he is an outstanding master, noble in nature, pleasant in his discourse. When you lead him, he leads obediently, and whatever you entrust to him, he suffices."
He said: Then Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) placed his hand on Zayd's shoulders and said: "This is your description, O Abu al-Husayn."

key_terms.سيد بارع: An outstanding master, a person who excels in all qualities
key_terms.طرائف: Gems, novelties, finest pieces of poetry

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about his brother Zayd ibn Ali?
ai.summary: In this gathering narrated by Jabir al-Ju'fi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) asked the poet Ma'ruf ibn Kharbudh al-Makki to recite some poetry. The poem praised a figure called Abu Malik for his strength, wisdom, noble character, pleasant speech, obedience in leadership, and reliability. Imam al-Baqir then turned to his brother Zayd ibn Ali and attributed these noble qualities to him, addressing him by his kunya Abu al-Husayn. This took place during the era of Imam al-Baqir (d. 114 AH), reflecting the Imam's esteem for his brother Zayd, who was known for his piety, courage, and later his uprising against the Umayyad caliphate.
